charts.title: fig10-2-executable-dynamics
charts.caption: Interactive: a biofilm assembles. Over 10 engine steps, biofilm_mass climbs 0 → 3.09, ecm 0 → 2.47, cells 1.00 → 2.09, and attached 0 → 1.85 — the individual cellular interfaces genuinely become part of a collective (biofilm) interface that couples to the environment as one composite (Law 2 preserved exactly). EXPLICIT caveat: this is a pattern demonstration, not a validated result — biofilm nesting is pre-declared from step 0 (a continuous scalar store, not discrete cell nodes inserted at runtime); the paper itself calls development/evolution "an open and substantial challenge."

charts.title: fig10-3-executable-dynamics
charts.caption: Interactive: a variant gains a new port. Over 10 engine steps, cell_O157.new_port ramps 0 → 0.65 (the dashed line marks it crossing 0.5, roughly its half-open point) while cell_ecoli.cell_count grows 1 → 4 under a fixed-constant selection ODE. EXPLICIT caveat: this is a pattern demonstration, not a validated result — selection is an ODE with viability and fitness held at fixed constants (not a real fitness landscape or genotype-driven differential fitness), and the new port is a config-driven first-order onset ramp (onset_rate=0.1), not an emergent evolutionary innovation; the paper itself calls this transition "an open and substantial challenge."
